source.author: verg
source.text: Pandarus ut fuso germanum corpore cernit et quo sit fortuna loco, qui casus agat res, portam vi magna converso cardine torquet, obnixus latis umeris, multosque suorum moenibus exclusos duro in certamine linquit; ast alios secum includit recipitque ruentis, demens, qui Rutulum in medio non agmine regem viderit irrumpentem ultroque incluserit urbi, immanem veluti pecora inter inertia tigrim Continuo nova lux oculis effulsit, et arma horrendum sonuere; tremunt in vertice cristae sanguineae, clipeoque micantia fulmina mittit:
source.text_original: Pandarus ut fuso germanum corpore cernit / et quo sit fortuna loco, qui casus agat res, / portam vi magna converso cardine torquet, / obnixus latis umeris, multosque suorum / moenibus exclusos duro in certamine linquit; / ast alios secum includit recipitque ruentis, / demens, qui Rutulum in medio non agmine regem / viderit irrumpentem ultroque incluserit urbi, / immanem veluti pecora inter inertia tigrim / Continuo nova lux oculis effulsit, et arma / horrendum sonuere; tremunt in vertice cristae / sanguineae, clipeoque micantia fulmina mittit: /
source.text_english: When Pandarus saw his brother’s body stretched out and in what place fortune stood, what chance was governing events, he twisted the gate on its turned hinge with great force, straining with his broad shoulders, and left many of his men shut out from the walls in the hard struggle; but others he shut in with himself and received as they rushed in, madman that he was, who had seen the Rutulian king breaking in among them with no battle line and had of his own accord shut him within the city, like a savage tiger among helpless cattle. At once a new light flashed in his eyes, and his arms sounded dreadfully; blood-red crests trembled on his head, and from his shield he sent flashing lightning:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tum validam contorto turbine portam impulit Hippotades.
reuse.text_original: tum validam contorto turbine portam / impulit Hippotades.
reuse.text_english: Then Hippotas’ son drove against the stout gate with a whirling blast.
